verdict.reason: Verified independently. The test mock at image-viewer.test.tsx:31 is `fetchDocuments: vi.fn(async () => [])`, so in image-viewer.tsx the `siblings` memo (lines 109-121) yields `[]`, `index = siblings.indexOf(documentId)` is -1 (line 123), and both `prevId` (line 124, requires `index > 0`) and `nextId` (lines 125-128, requires `index >= 0`) are `undefined`. `go` is `(id?) => id && navigate(...)` (lines 130-133), so it short-circuits. In the keydown handler (lines 139-154) the `if (hasOpenOverlay()) return;` guard at line 150 precedes the ArrowLeft/ArrowRight dispatch; with both ids undefined, removing that guard for arrow keys would not change the outcome, so `expect(navigate).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` at test line 99 after `fireEvent.keyDown(dialog, { key: "ArrowRight" })` (line 98) holds regardless of the behavior under test. The comment at test line 97 ("Arrow keys belong to the overlay too while it is open") presents this as coverage the assertion does not provide; the test also never awaits the sibling query before the keystroke. This is a vacuous assertion labeled as coverage of a guard branch — squarely in the test-adequacy lane and major by impact. The Esc half of the test is meaningful (positive control at lines 104-106), but that does not rescue the arrow-key assertion, and no guard or caller elsewhere makes it non-vacuous since nothing else in the rendered tree can invoke `navigate`.

verdict.reason: The capture-phase registration at image-viewer.tsx:155-156 is justified by the comment at lines 135-137 as being required because Radix's document-level handler unmounts a dismissable layer before a bubble-phase listener would see it. No test in the repository can distinguish capture from bubble. The only overlay fixture is a controlled, permanently-open `<Dialog open>` (image-viewer.test.tsx:56), whose own comment (lines 50-54) admits it "stays mounted"; hasOpenOverlay() (image-viewer.tsx:32-34) therefore returns true in either phase, so the assertions at lines 96 and 99 stay green with `, true)` reverted. The remaining three tests fire at window or a detached input with no overlay, so they are phase-insensitive. I searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide grep for ImageViewer (only file-detail.tsx/shared-document.tsx plus the two tests); file-detail.test.tsx:74 mocks ShareDialog to `() => null`, so the real dismissable overlay is never rendered there; no `addEventListener` spy exists in the frontend suite except an unrelated one at tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts:178; the repo's only real capture-phase assertion (packages/slides/test/view/present/presenter.test.ts:775-795) is for the slides presenter, a different component; and browser-level coverage (packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs, Escape at lines 581 and 1307) never touches the /f/:id viewer, with no e2e directory present. In-lane and blocking: the test's comment (lines 87-90) claims to cover the ShareDialog/Sheet dismissal case while using the one fixture where the phase cannot matter, i.e. coverage presented for a behavior it cannot fail on.

finding.summary: Share-link Esc test is vacuous — `expect(...).not.toThrow()` passes regardless of behavior
finding.evidence: The test titled "does nothing on Esc for a share-link viewer" only asserts `expect(() => fireEvent.keyDown(window, { key: 'Escape' })).not.toThrow()`. Dispatching a keydown never throws to the caller: jsdom catches exceptions raised inside event listeners and reports them as uncaught errors rather than propagating out of `dispatchEvent`. So this assertion holds whether the guard `onClose &&` exists or not, and even if the handler navigated away. It asserts nothing about the claimed behavior ("Esc must stay inert rather than navigate anywhere") — no navigation spy / route-location assertion is made.

verdict.reason: The described assertion does not exist. The test "does nothing on Esc for a share-link viewer, which has no list" (image-viewer.test.tsx:111-123) contains no `not.toThrow()` — a repo-wide grep for `not.toThrow` in packages/frontend/src finds it only in board-*.test.ts files and, in this file, only inside a comment (line 115) that explains why `not.toThrow()` would be inadequate. The real assertions are `expect(onError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (line 121), backed by a window `error` listener installed at lines 116-117, and `expect(navigate).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (line 122) against the `useNavigate` spy mocked at lines 9-16. That directly contradicts the claim that "no navigation spy / route-location assertion is made". The assertions are also non-vacuous against the code under test: image-viewer.tsx:153 is `else if (e.key === "Escape" && onClose) onClose();` — removing the `onClose &&` guard would invoke `undefined()` inside the capture-phase window listener registered at line 155, which jsdom surfaces as a window `error` event and would fail line 121; and navigation is performed via `navigate` (image-viewer.tsx:49, 131), the exact spy asserted on.
